questions.question: **Directions: In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'stereotype'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct spelling of the word is **'Stereotype'**
 
• **Stereotype **is a widely held and simplified belief or generalization about a particular group of people or things. It often involves assuming characteristics or behaviors based on limited or superficial knowledge, leading to unfair or inaccurate judgments.
 
 
• **Example**: The stereotype that all engineers are introverted and socially awkward is not true, as there are many outgoing and sociable engineers.
 
 
 
• The spelling of "**iliterrate**" is also incorrect. The correct spelling is "Illiterate".
 
• **Illiterate**: Illiterate refers to a person who lacks the ability to read and write. It describes someone who has not acquired basic literacy skills, which are necessary for understanding written language and communicating effectively through writing.
 
 
• **Example**: The high illiteracy rate in the rural community made it challenging for residents to access important information or engage in written communication.
 
 
 
• Hence option 2 is correct.

*So the correct sentence is- The fact that one has to be fiercely independent in this country was hard to get accustomed to.*

**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

I (have been advocate) moderation in daily physical exercise for nearly half a century in all my writings and books.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'have been advocating'**

• **According to grammar, **we use the present perfect continuous tense when something started in the past and is continuing at the present time. The present perfect continuous is formed using the construction has/have been + the present participle (root + -ing).
 
• **'For nearly half a century**' shows that the completion of the time. 
 
• The action that is 'advocating moderation' is still continuing in the present.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• I **have been reading** War and Peace for a month now.
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *I **have been advocating **moderation in daily physical exercise for nearly half a century in all my writings and books.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.**

Criticize in an abusive or angrily insulting manner
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Revile'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct answer for the best substitute of the words/sentence "**Criticize in an abusive or angrily insulting manner"** is: **Revile**.
 
• The word "**Revile**" accurately captures the meaning of criticizing someone in an abusive or angrily insulting manner. It refers to expressing strong, harsh, and disrespectful criticism towards someone, often accompanied by insults or offensive language.
 
 
• For example: "He was **reviled **by the media for his controversial remarks."
 
 
 
• Now, let's examine the other options:
 
• **Obeisance**: This option does not serve as a substitute for the given words/sentence. "Obeisance" refers to a gesture or action that shows respect, deference, or submission. It does not convey the idea of criticizing someone in an abusive or angrily insulting manner.
 
 
• Example: The subjects paid **obeisance **to the king by bowing before him.
 
 
 
• **Veneration**: This option is not the best substitute for the given words/sentence. "Veneration" means showing deep respect, admiration, or reverence towards someone or something. It does not carry the connotation of criticizing in an abusive or angrily insulting manner.
 
 
• Example: The ancient temple is held in high **veneration **by the local community.
 
 
 
• **Approbation**: This option does not accurately substitute the given words/sentence. "Approbation" refers to approval, praise, or favorable opinion about someone or something. It does not convey the idea of criticizing in an abusive or angrily insulting manner.
 
 
• Example: The committee gave their **approbation **to the proposed project.
 
 
 
• To summarize, the best substitute for the words/sentence** "Criticize in an abusive or angrily insulting manner"** is **"Revile," **as it specifically captures the meaning of harshly and disrespectfully criticizing someone. The other options, "Obeisance," "Veneration," and "Approbation," do not accurately represent the intended meaning.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

Meera said, “I prefer singing to dancing.”

options.text: Meera said that she preferred singing to dancing.
Meera say that she preferred singing to dancing.
Meera said she prefer singing to dancing.
Meera said that I prefer singing to dancing.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Meera said that she preferred singing to dancing.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

The given sentence is in 'Direct speech' we need to follow the following steps while changing Direct speech.

 
• #The first person of reported speech is changed according to the pronoun of the reporting verb.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• She said, "I will go to London." (Direct speech)
 
• She said that she would go to London. (Indirect speech)
 
 
 
• #The first-person pronoun of reported speech is not changed if the pronoun of the reporting verb is also the first person.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• I said, "I had applied for a job." (Direct speech.)
 
• I said I had applied for a job. (Indirect speech.)
 
 
 
• #The second person pronoun of the reported speech is changed according to the 'object' of the reporting verb.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• She said to me, "You are a brilliant student." (Direct Speech)
 
• She told me that I was a brilliant student. (Indirect Speech)
 
• She said to them, "You are brilliant students" (Direct speech)
 
• She told them that they are brilliant students. (Indirect speech)
 
 
 
• #The third person pronoun of the reported speech will not be changed in indirect speech.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• He said, "She will buy a pen." (Direct speech.)
 
• He said that she would buy a pen. (Indirect speech.)
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the verb 'prefer' is in the present simple tense hence, use the past simple in the indirect speech.

*So the correct answer is* **'option 1'**

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Disarming
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Detestable'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct answer for the word opposite in meaning to** "Disarming"** is: **Detestable**.
 
• The word "**Disarming**" refers to something that has the ability to remove suspicion, hostility, or fear, usually through charm, friendliness, or non-threatening behavior. It implies a sense of making others feel at ease, less guarded, or less defensive.
 
 
• For example, a disarming smile can make someone feel comfortable and open up in a conversation.
 
 
 
• On the other hand, "**Detestable**" is the opposite of "Disarming." It means deserving intense dislike, hatred, or strong aversion. When something or someone is described as detestable, it indicates that they are highly unpleasant, offensive, or repugnant.
 
 
• For instance, actions or behaviors that are considered morally repulsive or abhorrent can be described as detestable.
 
 
 
• Now, let's examine the other options:
 
• **Charming**: This option does not represent the opposite meaning of "Disarming" but rather a related concept. "Charming" refers to something or someone who has an attractive, pleasing, or charismatic quality. While charm can contribute to disarming someone, it is not the opposite of disarming.
 
• **Silk**: This option does not convey the opposite meaning of "Disarming." "Silk" refers to a type of fabric known for its softness and smoothness. It does not carry an opposite meaning in relation to "Disarming."
 
• **Convincing**: This option does not represent the opposite meaning of "Disarming" either. "Convincing" refers to something that is persuasive, compelling, or capable of causing someone to believe or be persuaded. It does not carry an opposite meaning to the concept of disarming.
 
• To summarize, the correct opposite for "**Disarming**" is "**Detestable**," as it denotes intense dislike or hatred. The other options, "**Charming**," "**Silk**," and "**Convincing**," do not represent the opposite meaning of "Disarming" but rather carry different meanings or related concepts.
